title: Working capital & lines of credit
metaDescription: Working capital financing can include business lines of credit, term loans, equipment financing, and invoice factoring for day-to-day cash flow and growth. Learn how these flexible structures differ.
summary: The working-capital page explains flexible financing options for day-to-day cash flow, recurring gaps, and shorter-term business needs.

hero.title: Working capital & lines of credit — stay flexible.
hero.lead: For cash-flow gaps, seasonality, and near-term needs, flexible financing may fit better than a long-term asset loan. Use this page to compare the common structures borrowers evaluate.

quickAnswer.definition: is short- to medium-term funding that covers day-to-day operating needs rather than long-term assets. It includes business lines of credit, term loans, equipment financing, and invoice factoring — each suited to different cash-flow situations.

whoItFits.heading: When working-capital options tend to fit
items: Smoothing seasonal or cyclical cash flow
Covering payroll, inventory, or supplier costs
Bridging the gap on outstanding invoices
Financing equipment over its useful life
Funding a specific, one-time growth project

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When working-capital options may not fit as well
items: Long-term fixed-asset projects may point more directly to SBA 504 or another asset-focused structure.
Borrowers seeking a larger acquisition or multi-purpose SBA structure may want to compare SBA 7(a) first.

typicalDocuments.heading: Typical documents lenders may request
items: Equipment or receivable details when applicable

howFund44Fits.heading: How Fund44 fits
howFund44Fits.summary: Fund44 helps a borrower compare flexible product structures and understand when a revolving or shorter-term path may fit better than a longer-term loan.
bullets: Puts lines of credit, term loans, equipment financing, and factoring into one comparison frame.
Connects flexible products to the same route and workflow.
Avoids promising provider speed or universal availability.

sectionDisclosureHtml: Fund44 is not a lender. Working-capital product availability, amounts, and terms are determined by third-party lenders and vary by provider. This page is educational only.

ctaBanner.heading: Need flexible cash flow?
ctaBanner.subheading: Preview lines of credit, term loans, and other working-capital paths based on your financing goal.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between a term loan and a line of credit?
commonQuestions.answer: A term loan gives you a fixed amount up front repaid on a set schedule — good for one-time needs. A line of credit lets you draw funds as needed up to a limit and repay as you go — good for recurring or unpredictable cash-flow gaps.

commonQuestions.question: How fast is working-capital financing?
commonQuestions.answer: Timelines vary by provider, product, and documentation. Fund44 does not guarantee any specific funding speed.

commonQuestions.question: What is invoice factoring?
commonQuestions.answer: Invoice factoring advances a portion of your outstanding invoices so you get cash sooner, with the factor collecting from your customers. It suits businesses with slow-paying B2B receivables.

commonQuestions.question: Does checking these options affect my credit?
commonQuestions.answer: Checking the preview uses information that does not affect your credit score because the current preview does not submit an application to a lender.
